text: Heads up team, deploying checkout-api v2.4.1 (commit a9f3c2) to prod-us-east-1 now. Changes include DB connection pooling tune and redis caching.
Sounds good @marcus.eng. Let me know if you need eyes on the canary pods.
Canary look clean. Rolling out to all 16 pods.
Rollout complete at 09:42 EDT. Health checks green. Keeping an eye on Datadog dashboard.
Updated cart-service rate limits config as well, no pods restarted, just config reload.
Is anyone seeing latency creeping up on the checkout funnel? Grafana P99 curve looks steep.
Checking the telemetry metrics now... looking at the graphs, it started at 14:02 UTC when latency began climbing.
Hey team, inventory-sync is buffering orders and queue is piling up unexpectedly. Seeing high response times calling checkout-api.
Wait, did anyone check if an alert fired? My Datadog tab has not refreshed.
<!channel> ALERT [4471] [CRITICAL] [E4] checkout-api P99 latency breach: 2840ms exceeds 2000ms threshold on /api/v1/checkout
<!channel> ALERT [4472] [CRITICAL] [E4] HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout rate spiked to 14.8% on checkout-api downstream dependencies
Seeing alert 4471. @sarah.triage can you please acknowledge alert 4471 and take Incident Commander?
Sarah is currently in an offsite meeting. I am stepping in and acknowledging alert 4471 now. I will act as Incident Commander for this SEV-1.
Incident INC-2026-001 officially declared. Impact: checkout degradation, error code E4, P99 latency > 2.8s. All triage to this thread.
Joining thread. I confirmed checkout latency began surging right around 14:02 UTC, though Datadog alert 4471 triggered at 14:07 UTC.
@marcus.eng What was deployed recently before this started?
I deployed checkout-api v2.4.1 (commit a9f3c2) at 09:40 EDT (~13:40 UTC). It made adjustments to the connection pool sizing and redis timeout.
Who deployed the database migration? Did someone run schema updates on postgres right before the incident?
Checking our CI/CD audit logs and deploy records: no database migration was deployed today. Only service code updates.
Confirming from infra side: no migration scripts or DDL statements executed against the database.
Let's inspect the active checkout-api connection pool metrics directly.
Here is the internal debug endpoint to inspect connection states:
Run this probe command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-FAKE-0000-TEST" https://checkout-api.internal/debug/pool/status
Output: active_connections: 64/64, queued_requests: 189, pool_exhausted: true. The new pool limit in commit a9f3c2 is choking under peak traffic.
Yes! The redis client timeout in v2.4.1 is holding connections indefinitely when redis throttles, causing error code E4 on checkout.
Agreed. Commit a9f3c2 is definitely the culprit.
ALERT [4474] [HIGH] [E8] Redis cache connection pool exhausted on checkout-api
ALERT [4476] [HIGH] [E19] Inventory-sync consumer group lag exceeded 10,000 messages (current: 14,210)
Root cause identified: connection pool and redis timeout misconfiguration introduced in commit a9f3c2 (v2.4.1).
We need an immediate rollback. @marcus.eng please rollback checkout-api to v2.4.0 (reverting a9f3c2).
Marcus is reviewing the core dump on server 4. I am executing the rollback of a9f3c2 right now via deploy runner (commit 7b1e4a).
Rollback triggered: checkout-api rolling back to v2.4.0 (commit 7b1e4a). Estimated pod replacement: 2 minutes.
Canary pods on v2.4.0 are coming online. Error rates dropping.
All 16 checkout-api pods are now running v2.4.0. Connection pool queued requests down from 189 to 0.
Rollback complete. All traffic served by v2.4.0. Checkout API P99 latency has dropped from 2840ms to 112ms.
RESOLVED: ALERT [4478] [INFO] checkout-api P99 latency returned to normal: 112ms (threshold: 2000ms)
RESOLVED: ALERT [4479] [INFO] Payment-gateway connection pool returned to baseline (18% utilized)
RESOLVED: ALERT [4480] [INFO] Inventory-sync queue drained to normal baseline (<50 messages)
Customer checkout conversions have fully rebounded. Error code E4 rate is 0.00%.
All systems nominal. Marking INC-2026-001 as RESOLVED at 10:35 EDT (~14:35 UTC). Post-mortem doc to follow.
Great turnaround everyone. Let us ensure load testing of connection pool sizes is mandatory in staging before v2.4.2.
Will document the post-mortem analysis and share with the team.
